goal.en: Take an argument apart fairly: what is claimed, what is shown, and what is merely assumed.
goal.ar: أن تفكّك الحجّة بإنصاف: ما المُدّعى، وما المُثبَت، وما المفترض دون دليل.

column.title: An opinion column
column.text:
Cities that introduced cycle lanes have seen a fall in traffic accidents. The conclusion is obvious: cycle lanes make roads safer, and every city should build them.

Critics complain about the cost. But you cannot put a price on a human life, and anyone who argues otherwise has misunderstood what a city is for. Either we accept a few weeks of roadworks, or we accept that people will continue to die on our streets. The choice could not be clearer.

My own street was rebuilt last year, and I have not seen a single accident since. That, more than any study, is what convinced me.

text.en: Every argument has three layers. The claim is what you are asked to accept; the evidence is what is offered; the assumption is the unstated step that connects them — and it is usually where the weakness lives.
text.ar: لكل حجّة ثلاث طبقات: الدعوى وهي ما يُطلب منك قبوله، والدليل وهو ما يُقدَّم، والافتراض وهو الخطوة غير المعلنة التي تربط بينهما — وفيها يكمن الضعف عادةً.

head: Layer
Question to ask
rows: What exactly am I being asked to believe?
What is offered, and how strong is it?
What must be true for the evidence to support the claim?
How far does the claim reach beyond the evidence?

text.en: The most useful critique names the assumption. Attacking the evidence invites a data argument; naming the assumption changes the conversation.
text.ar: أنفع نقدٍ هو الذي يسمّي الافتراض. فمهاجمة الدليل تجرّك إلى جدال في الأرقام، أما تسمية الافتراض فتغيّر مسار النقاش.

head: Move
What it does
Signal phrase
rows: cities that did X have seen Y
you cannot put a price on …

text.en: None of these makes a conclusion false. They make it unsupported — which is a different and more precise criticism.
text.ar: لا شيء من هذه يجعل النتيجة خاطئة، بل يجعلها غير مسنودة، وهذا نقد مختلف وأدقّ.

text.en: Naming a fallacy is not itself an argument. Say what the writer would need to show, not merely what they failed to show.
text.ar: تسمية المغالطة ليست حجّة بذاتها. فقل ما كان على الكاتب أن يُثبته، لا ما أخفق في إثباته فحسب.

head: Move
Language
rows: The evidence on X is convincing.
The difficulty is that this assumes …
A comparison with cities that did not … would help.
None of this shows the conclusion is wrong.

text.en: A critique that describes the argument accurately before attacking it is far harder to dismiss — and forces you to check you understood it.
text.ar: النقد الذي يصف الحجّة بدقة قبل مهاجمتها أصعب على الرفض بكثير، ويُلزمك بالتأكد من أنك فهمتها.

prompt.en: What assumption connects the evidence to the conclusion in paragraph one?
prompt.ar: ما الافتراض الذي يربط الدليل بالنتيجة في الفقرة الأولى؟

options: That the lanes caused the fall, and nothing else did.
That accidents were counted accurately in each city.
That cyclists prefer to ride in a marked lane.
That every city has the same amount of traffic.

explanation.en: The cities may have changed speed limits, enforcement or traffic volume at the same time.
explanation.ar: قد تكون تلك المدن غيّرت في الوقت نفسه حدود السرعة أو التطبيق أو كثافة المرور.

prompt.en: Which question best targets an argument's assumption?
prompt.ar: أي سؤال يستهدف افتراض الحجّة على نحو أفضل؟

options: What has to be true for this evidence to support this claim?
Who exactly funded the study that produced this evidence?
How many people currently agree with this conclusion?
When was the data behind this argument first collected?

explanation.en: That question exposes the hidden step; the others question the source or the age of the evidence.
explanation.ar: هذا السؤال يكشف الخطوة الخفية، أما البقية فتسائل مصدر الدليل أو قِدَمه.

prompt.en: The column says the conclusion is “obvious”. What does that word do here?

options: It substitutes confidence for the missing step in the argument.
It signals that a detailed proof follows immediately.
It concedes that other explanations are possible.
It limits the claim to the cities already studied.

explanation.en: “Obvious”, “clearly” and “of course” often mark the exact point where the reasoning was skipped.
explanation.ar: كلمات مثل obvious وclearly تشير غالباً إلى الموضع الذي قُفز فيه عن الاستدلال.

prompt.en: “Either we accept roadworks, or people continue to die.” What is wrong with this?

options: It presents two options as though no others exist.
It uses a tense that does not fit the meaning.
It quotes a study without naming its authors.
It repeats a point made in the first paragraph.

explanation.en: Enforcement, junction design and speed limits are among the options the sentence hides.
explanation.ar: تطبيق القانون وتصميم التقاطعات وحدود السرعة من الخيارات التي تخفيها الجملة.

prompt.en: What is the problem with “anyone who argues otherwise has misunderstood”?
prompt.ar: ما مشكلة عبارة anyone who argues otherwise has misunderstood؟

options: It discredits objectors instead of answering them.
It concedes too much ground to the critics.
It states the cost of the scheme inaccurately.
It introduces evidence from another country.

explanation.en: It makes disagreement a sign of stupidity, which removes the need to engage with it.
explanation.ar: تجعل الاعتراض دليل قصور في الفهم، فتُعفي الكاتب من الردّ عليه.

prompt.en: Why is the last paragraph the weakest evidence in the column?
prompt.ar: لماذا تُعدّ الفقرة الأخيرة أضعف دليل في المقال؟

options: One street over one year cannot establish a general effect.
The writer does not say which city the street is in.
It repeats the statistics given in the first paragraph.
It contradicts the claim made about cycle lanes.

explanation.en: The writer even ranks it above the studies — which is precisely the error.
explanation.ar: بل إن الكاتب يفضّلها على الدراسات، وهذا بعينه هو الخطأ.

prompt.en: Match the move with its description.

pairs: cities that did X saw Y

explanation.en: Each is a shortcut past the step the argument actually needed.
explanation.ar: كل واحدة منها قفزة فوق الخطوة التي كانت الحجّة تحتاجها فعلاً.

prompt.en: If an argument commits a fallacy, what follows?
prompt.ar: إذا وقعت حجّة في مغالطة، فماذا يترتب على ذلك؟

options: Its conclusion is unsupported, not necessarily false.
Its conclusion has been proved false by the fallacy.
Its evidence must have been fabricated deliberately.
Its author cannot be trusted on any subject at all.

explanation.en: A bad argument for a claim is not a disproof of it — a distinction careless critics lose.
explanation.ar: الحجّة الرديئة على دعوى ليست دحضاً لها، وهو تمييز يفقده النقاد المتعجّلون.

prompt.en: Which opening line of a critique is most likely to be taken seriously?
prompt.ar: أي افتتاحية نقدية أرجح أن تؤخذ بجدية؟

options: The argument holds that cycle lanes reduce accidents, and the correlation is real.
This column is a mess of fallacies from its first line to its very last.
I completely disagree with every single thing written in this column.
The writer clearly knows nothing at all about road safety in any city.

explanation.en: Describing the argument accurately first proves you understood it — and earns the right to criticise.
explanation.ar: وصف الحجّة بدقة أولاً يثبت أنك فهمتها، ويمنحك حق نقدها.

prompt.en: Which sentence names the gap most usefully?
prompt.ar: أي جملة تسمّي الثغرة بأنفع صورة؟

options: The difficulty is that this assumes nothing else changed at the same time.
The difficulty is that the writer is obviously biased about cycling.
The difficulty is that I have never seen a cycle lane work well.
The difficulty is that the column is far too short to be useful.

explanation.en: It states what must be true for the argument to work — a criticism the writer can actually answer.
explanation.ar: تذكر ما يجب أن يصحّ لتستقيم الحجّة، وهو نقد يستطيع الكاتب الردّ عليه فعلاً.

prompt.en: Which sentence says what would settle the question?
prompt.ar: أي جملة تبيّن ما يحسم المسألة؟

options: A comparison with similar cities that built no lanes would help.
More people should write about this important subject.
The writer should have been more polite to the critics.
Somebody ought to check whether the numbers are correct.

explanation.en: Naming the missing comparison turns a complaint into a research question.
explanation.ar: تسمية المقارنة الغائبة تحوّل الشكوى إلى سؤال بحثي.

prompt.en: Which closing sentence keeps a critique fair?

options: None of this shows the conclusion is wrong — only that it is unproven.
The column therefore has no value whatsoever to any reader.
It is clear that cycle lanes make no difference to safety.
The writer should retract the article and apologise for it.

explanation.en: Separating “unproven” from “false” is the whole discipline of critique in one sentence.
explanation.ar: التفريق بين «غير مُثبَت» و«خاطئ» هو جوهر النقد كله في جملة واحدة.

prompt.en: What claim does the column actually establish?
prompt.ar: ما الدعوى التي يثبتها المقال فعلاً؟

options: That accidents fell in cities which built lanes.
That cycle lanes are the cause of the fall.
That every city would benefit from lanes.
That the cost of the lanes is irrelevant.

explanation.en: The association is established; the cause and the general recommendation are not.
explanation.ar: الاقتران ثابت، أما السببية والتوصية العامة فغير ثابتتين.

prompt.en: “You cannot put a price on a human life.” Why is this hard to answer?
prompt.ar: لماذا يصعب الردّ على هذه العبارة؟

options: Disagreeing appears heartless, whatever the point being made.
It contains a statistic that cannot easily be checked.
It is written in a register that is far too formal.
It refers to a study that was apparently never published.

explanation.en: It converts a budgeting question into a moral test, which is exactly its function.
explanation.ar: تحوّل مسألة الميزانية إلى اختبار أخلاقي، وهذه وظيفتها بالضبط.

prompt.en: Complete the fair critique: “The evidence shows an association. The difficulty is that it ___ nothing else changed.”
prompt.ar: أكمل النقد المنصف: The difficulty is that it ___ nothing else changed.

explanation.en: Naming the assumption is the move that makes a critique constructive rather than dismissive.
explanation.ar: تسمية الافتراض هي الحركة التي تجعل النقد بنّاءً لا رافضاً.
